 Michael Malone makes powerful case for Cameron Fens in ongoing NCAA eligibility fight 
 The head coach of the Tar Heels is doing whatever he can to help Cameron Fens regain his eligibility. By Nick Delahanty | Nov 18, 2026, 9:27 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Oct 7, 2026; Charlotte, NC, USA; North Carolina Tar Heels head coach Michael Malone answers questions from the media during the ACC Tip-Off in Charlotte, NC. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Michael Malone isn't staying on the sidelines in Cameron Fens' ongoing eligibility battle with the NCAA.
--> Michael Malone isn't staying on the sidelines in Cameron Fens' ongoing eligibility battle with the NCAA.
 On Wednesday, Fens filed a motion for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction against the NCAA in Orange County Superior Court, continuing his pursuit of a fifth season of college eligibility.
--> On Wednesday, Fens filed a motion for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction against the NCAA in Orange County Superior Court, continuing his pursuit of a fifth season of college eligibility.
 However, the biggest development might be the involvement of Malone himself.
--> However, the biggest development might be the involvement of Malone himself.
 The head coach of the Tar Heels submitted an affidavit supporting Fens' request for a temporary restraining order. Signed on November 13, the document offers fascinating insight into how Malone views the situation and the impact Fens could have on his team.
--> The head coach of the Tar Heels submitted an affidavit supporting Fens' request for a temporary restraining order. Signed on November 13, the document offers fascinating insight into how Malone views the situation and the impact Fens could have on his team.
 Most notably, Malone made it abundantly clear that Fens would immediately join UNC's rotation if the legal process restores his eligibility.
--> Most notably, Malone made it abundantly clear that Fens would immediately join UNC's rotation if the legal process restores his eligibility.
 "If a court order bars the NCAA from treating Cameron as ineligible and from penalizing UNC, or Cameron's own records, because he played, UNC will certify his eligibility. Cameron is ready to play now. I will play him in our first game after he is certified."
--> "If a court order bars the NCAA from treating Cameron as ineligible and from penalizing UNC, or Cameron's own records, because he played, UNC will certify his eligibility. Cameron is ready to play now. I will play him in our first game after he is certified."
 That's about as definitive of a statement as Malone could make.
--> That's about as definitive of a statement as Malone could make.
 Fens has been practicing with the Tar Heels since arriving in August, participating in team activities and traveling with the program despite being unable to appear in games.
--> Fens has been practicing with the Tar Heels since arriving in August, participating in team activities and traveling with the program despite being unable to appear in games.
 While some might question how much impact the veteran center could have after missing time, Malone clearly believes Fens still has a role to play.
--> While some might question how much impact the veteran center could have after missing time, Malone clearly believes Fens still has a role to play.
 "He is physical and strong, and he is a skilled player. If he were eligible, he would be a regular part of our rotation."
--> "He is physical and strong, and he is a skilled player. If he were eligible, he would be a regular part of our rotation."
 Malone points to former Tar Heels in making his case
--> Malone points to former Tar Heels in making his case
 One of the most intriguing portions of Malone's affidavit involves two players UNC basketball fans know extremely well: Ven-Allen Lubin and Seth Trimble.
--> One of the most intriguing portions of Malone's affidavit involves two players UNC basketball fans know extremely well: Ven-Allen Lubin and Seth Trimble.
 Both players previously suited up for the Tar Heels before transferring elsewhere, and both are currently competing in their fifth seasons of college basketball.
--> Both players previously suited up for the Tar Heels before transferring elsewhere, and both are currently competing in their fifth seasons of college basketball.
 Lubin, who spent the 2024-2025 season in Chapel Hill, is now playing for NC State, while Trimble, who spent four seasons at UNC, is continuing his collegiate career at Louisville.
--> Lubin, who spent the 2024-2025 season in Chapel Hill, is now playing for NC State, while Trimble, who spent four seasons at UNC, is continuing his collegiate career at Louisville.
 Malone specifically mentioned both players while highlighting the circumstances surrounding Fens' eligibility battle.
--> Malone specifically mentioned both players while highlighting the circumstances surrounding Fens' eligibility battle.
 "NC State, which we play on December 15 and January 9, has Ven-Allen Lubin, who played the 2024-25 season here at North Carolina before I arrived and is now in his fifth college season. Louisville, which we play on January 5 and February 8, has Seth Trimble, who played four seasons here at North Carolina before I arrived and is now playing a fifth season for Louisville."
--> "NC State, which we play on December 15 and January 9, has Ven-Allen Lubin, who played the 2024-25 season here at North Carolina before I arrived and is now in his fifth college season. Louisville, which we play on January 5 and February 8, has Seth Trimble, who played four seasons here at North Carolina before I arrived and is now playing a fifth season for Louisville."
 The significance of those examples goes beyond their previous connections to North Carolina.
--> The significance of those examples goes beyond their previous connections to North Carolina.
 Malone identified several other fifth-year players on North Carolina's schedule, including West Virginia's Brenen Lorient and Javan Buchanan, Syracuse's Amarri Monroe, Wake Forest's Justin Abson, and Miami's Malik Reneau.
--> Malone identified several other fifth-year players on North Carolina's schedule, including West Virginia's Brenen Lorient and Javan Buchanan, Syracuse's Amarri Monroe, Wake Forest's Justin Abson, and Miami's Malik Reneau.
 His argument is straightforward: UNC is preparing to face opponents who have players competing under court orders, while Fens remains unable to take the floor.
--> His argument is straightforward: UNC is preparing to face opponents who have players competing under court orders, while Fens remains unable to take the floor.
 "Playing Cameron would put him on the same footing as the fifth-year players we will compete against."
--> "Playing Cameron would put him on the same footing as the fifth-year players we will compete against."
 Like all of us, Malone is still trying to figure out why his guy is ineligible while others are granted the opportunity to play.
--> Like all of us, Malone is still trying to figure out why his guy is ineligible while others are granted the opportunity to play.
 The Tar Heels could find themselves competing against Lubin and Trimble later this season while their own fifth-year eligibility candidate continues fighting for the opportunity to play.
--> The Tar Heels could find themselves competing against Lubin and Trimble later this season while their own fifth-year eligibility candidate continues fighting for the opportunity to play.
 Make it make sense!
--> Make it make sense!
 Malone explains why the situation extends beyond basketball
--> Malone explains why the situation extends beyond basketball
 Malone also addressed the potential consequences of playing Fens without sufficient protection against NCAA penalties. He explained that the NCAA could potentially penalize North Carolina if a court order permitting Fens to compete were later overturned, including vacating victories and jeopardizing postseason eligibility.
--> Malone also addressed the potential consequences of playing Fens without sufficient protection against NCAA penalties. He explained that the NCAA could potentially penalize North Carolina if a court order permitting Fens to compete were later overturned, including vacating victories and jeopardizing postseason eligibility.
 He made it abundantly clear that he isn't willing to put his entire team in that position.
--> He made it abundantly clear that he isn't willing to put his entire team in that position.
 "I would not ask my players to play games that could be taken from them after the fact. They earn their wins on the court. UNC will not play Cameron under an order that leaves that rule in place."
--> "I would not ask my players to play games that could be taken from them after the fact. They earn their wins on the court. UNC will not play Cameron under an order that leaves that rule in place."
 Malone also emphasized how Fens' inability to compete could affect his professional basketball aspirations.
--> Malone also emphasized how Fens' inability to compete could affect his professional basketball aspirations.
 Drawing upon his NBA coaching experience, Malone explained that professional organizations need to evaluate how players perform against high-level competition. For Fens, who previously competed at South Dakota, this season represents an opportunity to demonstrate his abilities against some of the nation's most talented programs.
--> Drawing upon his NBA coaching experience, Malone explained that professional organizations need to evaluate how players perform against high-level competition. For Fens, who previously competed at South Dakota, this season represents an opportunity to demonstrate his abilities against some of the nation's most talented programs.
 "Only games against teams like Kentucky, Arkansas, and Duke can answer it. This season is his last to answer that question at this level, and each game he misses takes part of that chance away."
--> "Only games against teams like Kentucky, Arkansas, and Duke can answer it. This season is his last to answer that question at this level, and each game he misses takes part of that chance away."
 Perhaps the most meaningful statement, though, came at the conclusion of his affidavit.
--> Perhaps the most meaningful statement, though, came at the conclusion of his affidavit.
 "Cameron has done everything we have asked of him since he arrived. He belongs to this team, and he should be allowed to play for it."
--> "Cameron has done everything we have asked of him since he arrived. He belongs to this team, and he should be allowed to play for it."
 Those words speak volumes about Malone's support for his player.
--> Those words speak volumes about Malone's support for his player.
 While there is still no guarantee that Fens will ultimately receive the legal relief necessary to compete, Michael Malone has made his position unmistakably clear.
--> While there is still no guarantee that Fens will ultimately receive the legal relief necessary to compete, Michael Malone has made his position unmistakably clear.
 If Fens receives the necessary clearance and protections, Malone won't waste any time getting him onto the court. UNC is simply waiting for the green light.
--> If Fens receives the necessary clearance and protections, Malone won't waste any time getting him onto the court. UNC is simply waiting for the green light.
